The command keeps running after this call returns and after the caller's
connection drops: erun gives it its own session and captures its merged
stdout and stderr to the job's log, so nothing has to be wrapped in setsid,
nohup, or a redirect.

The exit status is recorded by the process that waits on the work, inside
the environment, so no sentinel token and no shell expansion sit between the
work and its result. The id defaults to the name; re-using the id of a job
that is still running is refused, while re-using a finished one replaces it.

--agent runs an AI tool instead of a command, with the trailing arguments as
the prompt. erun invokes the tool in its streaming mode, which is what makes
an agent run observable at all: left to its default the tool prints nothing
until it exits, so a multi-hour run reports no output while it is actively
editing files. status then reports the current activity, not only "running".

--env sets additional environment for the job's own process, on top of what
it inherits from the environment's runtime pod — for example raising
CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS for one agent run. Values land in the job
supervisor's argv, visible to anything that can list processes in this
environment, so this is not where secrets belong; PATH, LD_PRELOAD, and a
few other names that could redirect what the job executes are refused.

Usage:
  erun job start [flags] -- <command> [args...]

Examples:
  # Start a test suite and come back for the result.
  erun job start --tenant team --environment dev --name suite -- ./gradlew test
  erun job await --tenant team --environment dev --id suite --timeout 5m

  # Start an agent and watch what it is doing.
  erun job start --tenant team --environment dev --name sweep --agent claude -- 'fix the failing tests'
  erun job status --tenant team --environment dev --id sweep

  # Raise an agent's output-token cap for this run only.
  erun job start --tenant team --environment dev --name sweep --agent claude \
    --env CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=64000 -- 'rewrite the module'

Flags:
      --agent string           Run an AI tool (claude or codex) in streaming mode, taking the trailing arguments as its prompt
      --dir string             Working directory in the environment to run the command from
      --dry-run                Resolve and trace mutating actions without executing them.
      --env stringArray        Additional KEY=VALUE environment for the job's process; repeat for several. Not for secrets: values are visible in the job supervisor's argv
      --environment string     Environment the job runs in
  -h, --help                   help for start
      --id string              Handle to address the job by (defaults to the name)
      --lease-ttl duration     Activity lease TTL the job renews inside while it runs (default 15m0s)
      --max-output-bytes int   Cap on captured output; past it output is dropped and the job says so (default 16777216)
      --name string            What the work is, shown wherever the environment reports as busy
      --tenant string          Tenant whose environment the job belongs to

Global Flags:
      --output string   Result format: text (default, human stream) or json (structured result on stdout for orchestrators). (default "text")
      --time            Print the elapsed runtime after the command finishes.
  -v, --verbose count   Increase verbosity: -v streams external tool output, -vv adds erun command traces.
